correctness.rationale: The support of nonzero spectral rectangular compressions is compact and nonempty. A finite spectral grid with aspect <=1+epsilon and the ideal p-quasi-triangle bound controls limsup by the max ratio; a nonzero compression around any support point controls liminf by its local ratio. Both directions give true root limits, independent of p. Diagonal-only spectral coupling forces every separated compression to vanish, hence intertwining by spectral projection approximation. Fresh 30 finite-matrix Schatten root comparisons and a nontrivial intertwiner example corroborate, not prove, the infinite-dimensional result.
residual_risks: Finite calculations are not universal proofs; precise proof lemmas assessed separately.
